strategy_title: Larger XBLOCK autotune regresses due to instruction bloat
strategy_description: Increasing XBLOCK from 128 to 512–2048 via autotune doubled register usage (17→32 registers/thread) and more than doubled total executed instructions (9.3M→19.9M), causing a 40% slowdown despite improving achieved occupancy (56%→87%) and compute throughput (54%→83%). The L1/TEX hit rate dropped from 83% to 66%, indicating that larger tiles caused cache thrashing on the per-channel broadcast tensors (size 32) accessed via modulo indexing. The net effect was that the extra instruction count and cache pressure outweighed the latency-hiding benefit of higher occupancy, resulting in a longer kernel duration (21.9 µs→30.7 µs). When a kernel already has high L1 hit rate on small broadcast tensors and moderate compute throughput, increasing tile size can destroy cache locality and inflate instruction count without proportional throughput gain.
slow_pseudocode:
# XBLOCK=128, 17 regs/thread, 9.3M instructions, L1 hit=83%, duration=21.9us
@triton.jit
def kernel(in_out_ptr0, in_ptr0..3, xnumel, XBLOCK: tl.constexpr):
    xindex = tl.program_id(0) * XBLOCK + tl.arange(0, XBLOCK)
    xmask = tl.full([XBLOCK], True, tl.int1)
    x0 = xindex % 32  # channel index into small broadcast tensors
    tmp0 = tl.load(in_out_ptr0 + xindex, None)
    tmp1 = tl.load(in_ptr0 + x0, None, eviction_policy='evict_last')
    # ... batch norm + hardtanh ...
    tl.store(in_out_ptr0 + xindex, result, None)
grid = (cdiv(xnumel, 128),)
fast_pseudocode:
# XBLOCK autotuned {512,1024,2048}, 32 regs/thread, 19.9M instructions, L1 hit=66%, duration=30.7us
@triton.autotune(configs=[Config({'XBLOCK':512},num_warps=4), ...Config({'XBLOCK':2048},num_warps=32)], key=['xnumel'])
@triton.jit
def kernel(in_out_ptr0, in_ptr0..3, xnumel, XBLOCK: tl.constexpr):
    xindex = tl.program_id(0) * XBLOCK + tl.arange(0, XBLOCK)
    xmask = xindex < xnumel
    x0 = xindex % 32
    tmp0 = tl.load(in_out_ptr0 + xindex, xmask)
    tmp1 = tl.load(in_ptr0 + x0, xmask, eviction_policy='evict_last')
    # ... batch norm + hardtanh ...
    tl.store(in_out_ptr0 + xindex, result, xmask)
grid = lambda meta: (cdiv(xnumel, meta['XBLOCK']),)
applicable_when: Never beneficial in this configuration; generally avoid when small broadcast tensors (e.g., per-channel BN params) are accessed via modulo indexing and already have high L1 hit rate (>80%), and when register count is near the block-limit-register boundary.
do_not_apply_when: Kernel has high L1/TEX hit rate (>75%) on small broadcast tensors accessed via modulo; kernel is already achieving moderate compute throughput (>50%); increasing XBLOCK would double register usage and push block-limit-registers lower, reducing effective occupancy ceiling; total instruction count scales super-linearly with XBLOCK due to predicated/masked operations.
framework_notes: In Triton, adding @triton.autotune with larger XBLOCK configs causes the compiler to allocate more registers per thread (17→32 in this case), which halves the Block Limit Registers (21→16 blocks/SM). The xmask predication on all loads/stores also adds instruction overhead that compounds with larger XBLOCK. The grid must be updated to lambda meta: (cdiv(xnumel, meta['XBLOCK']),) when using autotune, but the static grid=(cdiv(xnumel,128),) in kernel_function was not updated, meaning autotune configs with XBLOCK>128 would use an oversized grid — this implementation flaw may have contributed to the regression.
